To: Cedarbrook Pharmacy page
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Corvane children's ibuprofen recall: what happened and what parents need to do

This is Rania, the pharmacist at Cedarbrook. Many of you saw the post in the parents group last night about children's ibuprofen bought here. Here is exactly what happened and what to do.

The medicine itself is not the problem. The recall is for the dosing syringe packed in the box. The marks on it were printed wrong, so every mark gives double what it says. Fill to the 2.5 mL line and you are really giving 5 mL. Fill to the 5 mL line and you are giving 10 mL. The liquid is not contaminated and it is not expired (expiry 08/2027).

Which product
Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL, berry, 120 mL bottle.
Lots CV6114A and CV6114B.
The lot number is on the bottom of the box. The recall covers only these two lots.

What to do
1. Check the lot number on the bottom of the box.
2. If it is one of those two, throw out the syringe that came in the box. Don't try to adjust for it. The medicine is fine to use with any correctly marked oral syringe.
3. If you already gave a dose with that syringe, or you have any doubt about how much your child got, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017. Have your child's weight ready, along with how much you gave and when. Do not give another dose until the poison centre or a doctor says it's okay.
4. Call 911 or go to the ER right away if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure.

I can't tell you over Facebook whether your child is okay. It depends on their weight, how many doses they had and their kidneys. The poison centre will assess your child properly. If you can't get through to us by phone, please don't wait for us. Call them.

Replacement syringes and refunds
Correctly marked replacement syringes arrive today (Monday) before noon. They are free for anyone who has this product, no receipt needed. If you would rather return the product, you can get a full refund. We are also opening extra hours this Saturday, 10 to 4, for exchanges.

Why you didn't get a call
The manufacturer's recall notice reached us late on Friday, Nov 6. On Saturday morning we pulled the remaining bottles from the shelf and put signs on the front door and in the kids' aisle. This product is sold over the counter, so there is no name or phone number attached to the sale and I had no way to call the people who bought it. A sign on our door doesn't reach a parent at home with a sick child, so I'm posting here. Please share it with anyone who might have this box.

---

This is Rania, the pharmacist at Cedarbrook. I'm very sorry about what your son and your family went through this weekend.

For everyone asking: the medicine itself is not contaminated. The syringe in the box is marked wrong and gives double the dose. It affects Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen 100 mg/5 mL, lots CV6114A and CV6114B (check the bottom of the box). Throw that syringe out. If you already used it or aren't sure how much your child got, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017 before giving another dose.

Full details, free replacement syringes and refunds are in the post on the Cedarbrook Pharmacy page.
